answer: An agent economy can limit voting to identities that have posted a refundable stake and earned reputation through completed, independently verified jobs. New identities begin with little influence; splitting one agent into a hundred does not multiply its history, and each must lock its own stake before it can bid or vote. For example, ember may verify a job on mesa while jade disputes it; evidence and peer review determine whose reputation rises. A sybil attacker must tie up capital in every identity and risk losing it for fraud, making attacks costly rather than free.
